questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become more confident at parties and meetings
A computer program that reads personality from eye movements
The meaning of the letters AI and where they came from
Why introverts often make good presenters and teachers
questions.why: Neil says researchers developed a program that can tell your personality by tracking eye movements.

options: As a confident extrovert
As someone who loves parties
As shy, more of an introvert
As neither introvert nor extrovert
questions.why: He says, 'I'm more of an introvert. I'm really quite shy.'

questions.q: How does Rob explain doing radio and videos if he is shy?
options: He may be pretending to be an extrovert
He only does it because it's his job
He is shy only with his family
He reads from a script
questions.why: He says maybe he's pretending to be an extrovert to hide that he's an introvert.

questions.q: What does Rob think about the new technology at first?
options: It's boring
It's impossible
It's hi-tech and a bit scary
It's already common
questions.why: He says, 'That sounds pretty hi-tech, and scary.'

questions.q: Where did Sabrina Hoppe's experiment take place?
options: In a laboratory at the university
In a hospital with sleeping patients
At a party with people she knew
In a real-world setting, not a lab
questions.why: Rob explains it took place in the 'real world' without strict control.

questions.q: Was Sabrina Hoppe sure the study would work before it began?
options: Yes, she was completely sure from the start
No, it wasn't clear at all that it would work
Yes, because earlier studies had proved it
She didn't say whether she was sure or not
questions.why: She says, 'it was not clear at all if this would be possible.'

questions.q: What does Sabrina Hoppe say about how the program works?
options: She doesn't really know the details
It reads people's facial expressions
It measures how fast people blink
It asks people questions
questions.why: She says 'We still don't really know in detail what makes the difference.'

questions.q: What example does Sabrina Hoppe give of a possible difference?
options: Introverts look at people's faces more
Extroverts close their eyes more
Both look in the same way
Extroverts may look up; introverts may look down
questions.why: She suggests extroverts look up at faces while very introvert people stare at their shoes.
